title: Resampling
summary: Group a time series into days, weeks or months with resample, and fill the gaps.

steps.title: resample: groupby for time
body: Orders arrive at random moments; questions are asked per day, week or month. `resample` groups a time-indexed
Series or DataFrame into **regular buckets** and aggregates each one:
s.resample("W").sum()     # per week, labelled by the Sunday that ends it
s.resample("ME").sum()    # per month, labelled by the month END (2024-01-31)
s.resample("MS").sum()    # per month, labelled by the month START (2024-01-01)
Unlike `groupby`, every bucket between the first and last date appears, even empty ones: `sum` gives 0 there,
`mean` gives NaN. That makes gaps visible instead of silently missing.

steps.prompt: `s` has daily values for January 2024. What is the index label of the single row of `s.resample("ME").sum()`?
steps.explain: `ME` means month end, so buckets are labelled with their last day. Use `MS` for the first day.

steps.prompt: 1 January 2024 was a Monday. What does this print?
steps.explain: Monday 1st to Sunday 7th hold 1..7 (sum 28); the 8th to 10th hold 8, 9, 10 (27). Weekly buckets are labelled by their Sunday.

steps.title: Choosing the aggregation
body: The bucket is only half the decision; the other half is **how to combine** the values in it:
| flows: revenue, visits, units sold | `sum` | a month's revenue is all its days added up |
| levels: temperature, price, wait time | `mean` | adding temperatures means nothing |
| stocks: balance, inventory | `last` | the month-end balance is the last one seen |
Ask for several at once with `.agg(["sum", "mean", "count"])` or named: `.agg(total="sum", orders="count")`.
Going the other way, `s.asfreq("D")` **upsamples**: it inserts a row for every missing day (as NaN), which you then
fill with `fillna(0)` (no sales happened) or `ffill()` (the last reading still holds).

steps.prompt: How should each daily quantity be combined into a monthly figure?
items: bank balance at close of day
steps.explain: Flows add up, levels average, stocks take the latest value.

steps.title: Monthly revenue
prompt: Write `monthly_revenue(df)`. `df` has a `date` column (already datetimes) and a `revenue` column, one row per order,
in any order. Return a Series of total revenue **per calendar month**, labelled by month end, with every month between the
first and last order (0 for a month with none).
hints: Set the date as the index first: `df.set_index("date")`.
template: Dojo.eq("monthly totals", [11.0, 0.0, 30.0], [float(round(v, 2)) for v in dojo_m.tolist()])

steps.explain: `asfreq` adds 2 and 3 January as NaN (which turns the values into floats). `fillna(0)` says nothing happened; `ffill` carries 5 forward.

steps.prompt: Arrange the lines to print the weekly average temperature from a table with text timestamps.

steps.title: No missing days
prompt: Write `daily_counts(df)`. `df` has one row per order and a `date` column of datetimes (any order, possibly several per day,
and some days with no orders). Return a Series with **one entry per day** from the first to the last date holding the
number of orders that day, 0 on days without any.
hints: `groupby` only returns the days that exist. `resample` returns every day in the range.
`.resample("D").size()` counts rows per day, giving 0 for empty days.
template: Dojo.eq("six days from 1 to 6 May", 6, len(dojo_c))
Dojo.eq("counts per day", [1, 0, 3, 0, 0, 1], [int(v) for v in dojo_c.tolist()])

steps.title: Monthly summary
prompt: Write `monthly_summary(df)`. `df` has `date` (datetimes) and `revenue`. Return a DataFrame indexed by month end with three
- `average`: the mean revenue per order, rounded to 2 decimals,
Months with no orders should still appear (total 0, orders 0).
hints: Named aggregation works on a resample: `.agg(total="sum", average="mean", orders="count")`.
